title: Mail Memories – A desktop app to rescue photos from Gmail
claim: Show HN: Mail Memories – A desktop app to rescue photos from Gmail
why_good: A desktop app to extract and rescue photos buried in Gmail — a real, relatable pain (photos trapped in email) with a clear job-to-be-done.
value: Anyone changing phones, retiring an old mailbox, or sorting out a late relative's accounts. One-time purchase.
risk: A single-use utility with no repeat, on a job the platform can absorb in one release.

zh.claim: Show HN: Mail Memories —— 从 Gmail 里抢救照片的桌面 app。
zh.why_good: 一个把埋在 Gmail 里的照片提取、抢救出来的桌面 app——真实、有共鸣的痛点,要做的事清晰。
zh.value: 换手机、注销旧邮箱、整理过世亲人账号的普通人；一次性买断。
zh.risk: 一次性工具，零复购，而平台一个勾选框就能替代。
zh.hook: 同一个邮箱用了十五年的人：家里还留着的照片有相当一部分只存在于附件里——某次出生、某次葬礼、爸妈扫描过来的一张纸——散在几千封邮件中间。Google Takeout 导出来是一坨谁也打不开的 .mbox。
zh.does: 一个本地桌面程序，扫过整个邮箱，把附件里的照片抽出来、去重，按日期排成普通的相册文件夹。全程不上传。
zh.gap: Takeout 交付的是归档格式不是相册；Google Photos 只认你主动上传过的，认不出你 2011 年发给自己的那张扫描件。缺的是最后一公里的解包，不是导出。
zh.counter: 这是一次性的活，打开一次就不再打开；而 Google 只要在 Takeout 后面加一个「照片文件夹」勾选框就能一夜抹掉它。它还天然要拿邮箱权限——普通人对这件事最敏感。
zh.differentiator: 把「只在本机」做成产品本身而不是脚注：只读、不联网，产物是一个能直接拖进手机相册的文件夹，外加一页「这些照片里出现最多的十张脸」。冷启动：中文=小红书/豆瓣「邮箱 老照片 找回」「换手机 照片丢了」；英文=r/DataHoarder 与 r/gmail 每隔几个月复现的 how do I get ten years of attachments out 帖。
zh.edge: 它把邮箱当相册读，而不是当邮件读：十几年里大家互相寄来寄去的照片，被挖出来、按时间排好，全部在本机完成，不上传。
zh.why_use: 对那些在手机相册自动同步之前就上网的人来说，一张家庭照片唯一还活着的副本，往往就是一封谁也再找不到的邮件附件。
zh.consumer_angle: 一个有十五年历史邮箱的人，完全不知道哪一封信里躺着爸妈那张照片的唯一副本。

hook: Someone who has used the same mailbox for fifteen years: a large share of the family photos they still own exist only as email attachments — a birth, a funeral, a scanned document from a parent — scattered across thousands of messages. Google Takeout hands back a .mbox nobody can open.
does: A local desktop app that walks the whole mailbox, pulls the photos out of attachments, de-duplicates them, and lays them out as ordinary dated album folders. Nothing is uploaded.
gap: Takeout delivers an archive format, not an album; Google Photos only knows what you deliberately uploaded, and cannot see the scan you emailed yourself in 2011. The missing piece is the last-mile unpacking, not the export.
counter: It is a one-time job — opened once, never again — and Google closes it forever by adding a single 'photos folder' checkbox to Takeout. It also has to ask for mailbox access, which is the permission ordinary people are most reluctant to grant.
differentiator: Make local-only the product, not a footnote: read-only, no network, and the deliverable is a folder you can drag straight into a phone gallery plus a contact sheet of the ten faces that appear most. Cold start (Chinese): 小红书/豆瓣 「邮箱 老照片 找回」「换手机 照片丢了」; (English): the 'how do I get ten years of attachments out of Gmail' thread that recurs in r/DataHoarder and r/gmail.
consumer_angle: A non-technical person with a decade-old mailbox; the deliverable is an album folder they can actually open.
edge: It reads the mailbox as a photo archive rather than as mail: a decade of pictures people mailed each other, pulled out and dated, on the machine, with no upload.
why_use: For anyone who was online before phone galleries synced, the only surviving copy of a family photo is often an email attachment nobody can find any more.
